item.title: Interview: Congo’s Foreign Minister on the Gaps Between Diplomacy and War at Home

item.title: ‘Wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain’ by gangs in Haiti
item.description: Gangs in Haiti continue to terrorize communities with the “wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain” on people who often are just in the wrong place at the wrong time.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Warnings of famine and collapse as South Sudan's peace deal frays
item.description: Nearly eight million people in South Sudan – more than half the population – face crisis-level hunger, with famine risk now flagged in four counties, as the Security Council meets this morning in New York. A cholera outbreak has killed more than 1,700 people, and some aid workers are being killed and abducted even as they try to reach those most at risk. Follow live coverage below.

item.title: Gaza: 300 children killed in 300 days of Israeli-Hamas ‘ceasefire’
item.description: At least 300 children in Gaza have been reportedly killed in as many days since a ceasefire agreement came into effect last October to suspend military operations between Hamas fighters and the Israel Defense Forces, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Thursday.

item.title: Cuba: Independent experts condemn new US sanctions as humanitarian crisis deepens
item.description: Independent UN human rights experts on Thursday condemned a fresh round of US sanctions against Cuba, calling them an attempt to force change on “a sovereign State through threats and coercion.”

item.title: Ebola virus reaches displacement camps in DR Congo
item.description: Agencies are on high alert amid reports that the rapidly spreading Ebola Bundibugyo virus species in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has infected 19 internally displaced people, killed five of them, according to the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR).

item.title: The Year of Pastoralists Must Be More Than Symbolic
item.description: This is supposed to be the year the world finally sees and recognizes pastoralists. The United Nations has designated 2026 as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists, bringing long-overdue attention to communities who have sustained some of the world’s most fragile and important landscapes for generations.
